{{Short description|Manifold equipped with a quaternionic structure}}
In [[differential geometry]], a '''hypercomplex manifold''' is a [[manifold]] with the [[tangent bundle]]
equipped with an [[Module (mathematics)|action]] by [[Quaternions|the algebra of quaternions]]
in such a way that the quaternions <math>I, J, K</math>
define integrable [[Almost complex manifold|almost complex structures]].

If the almost complex structures are instead not assumed to be integrable, the manifold is called quaternionic, or almost hypercomplex.<ref>{{Cite book|arxiv=0804.2814|last1=Manev|first1=Mancho|title=Contemporary Aspects of Complex Analysis, Differential Geometry and Mathematical Physics|editor= S. Dimiev and K. Sekigawa|publisher= World Sci. Publ.|location= Hackensack, NJ |volume=2005|pages=174–186|last2=Sekigawa|first2=Kouei|doi=10.1142/9789812701763_0016|chapter=Some Four-Dimensional Almost Hypercomplex Pseudo-Hermitian Manifolds|date=2005 |isbn=978-981-256-390-3}}</ref>

== Examples ==

Every [[hyperkähler manifold]] is also hypercomplex.
The converse is not true. The [[Hopf surface]]
:<math>\bigg({\mathbb H}\backslash 0\bigg)/{\mathbb Z}</math> 
(with <math>{\mathbb Z}</math> acting
as a multiplication by a quaternion <math>q</math>, <math>|q|>1</math>) is
hypercomplex, but not [[Kähler manifold|Kähler]],
hence not [[Hyperkähler manifold|hyperkähler]] either.
To see that the Hopf surface is not Kähler,
notice that it is [[Diffeomorphism|diffeomorphic]] to a product
<math>S^1\times S^3,</math> hence its odd cohomology
group is odd-dimensional. By [[Hodge decomposition]],
odd cohomology of a compact [[Kähler manifold]]
are always even-dimensional. In fact Hidekiyo Wakakuwa proved
<ref>
 {{citation |first =Hidekiyo| last =  Wakakuwa |  title =On Riemannian manifolds with homogeneous holonomy group Sp(n)| volume =10| issue = 3 | journal = [[Tôhoku Mathematical Journal]]|year =1958| pages =274–303 | doi=10.2748/tmj/1178244665| doi-access =free}}. 
</ref> that on a compact [[hyperkähler manifold]] <math>\ b_{2p+1}\equiv 0  \  mod \ 4</math>. 
[[Misha Verbitsky]] has shown that any compact
hypercomplex manifold admitting a Kähler structure is also hyperkähler.<ref>{{citation |first = Misha| last = Verbitsky| authorlink= Misha Verbitsky | title =Hypercomplex structures on Kaehler manifolds | volume =15 | issue = 6| journal = GAFA|year =2005| pages =1275–1283 | doi=10.1007/s00039-005-0537-4| arxiv =math/0406390}}</ref>

In 1988, left-invariant hypercomplex structures on some compact [[Lie group]]s
were constructed by the physicists Philippe Spindel, Alexander Sevrin, Walter Troost, and Antoine Van Proeyen. In 1992, [[Dominic Joyce]] 
rediscovered this construction, and gave a complete classification of 
left-invariant hypercomplex structures on compact Lie groups. 
Here is the complete list.

:<math>
T^4, SU(2l+1), T^1 \times SU(2l), T^l \times SO(2l+1),
</math> 
:<math>T^{2l}\times SO(4l), T^l \times Sp(l), T^2 \times E_6,</math> 
:<math>
T^7\times E^7, T^8\times E^8, T^4\times F_4, T^2\times G_2
</math>

where <math>T^i</math> denotes an <math>i</math>-dimensional compact torus.

It is remarkable that any [[Compact group|compact Lie group]] becomes
hypercomplex after it is multiplied by a sufficiently
big torus.

== Basic properties ==

Hypercomplex manifolds as such were studied by Charles Boyer in 1988. He also proved that in real dimension 4, the only compact hypercomplex
manifolds are the complex torus <math>T^4</math>, the [[Hopf surface]] and 
the [[K3 surface]].

Much earlier (in 1955) [[Morio Obata]] studied [[affine connection]] associated with ''almost hypercomplex structures'' (under the former terminology of [[Charles Ehresmann]]<ref>{{citation | first =Charles| last =Ehresmann| authorlink=Edmond Bonan | title =Sur la théorie des espaces fibrés| journal = Coll. Top. Alg., Paris | year =1947 }}.</ref> of ''almost quaternionic structures''). His construction leads to what [[Edmond Bonan]] called the ''Obata connection''<ref>{{citation | first =Edmond| last =Bonan | authorlink=Edmond Bonan | title =Tenseur de structure d'une variété presque quaternionienne | journal = C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris | volume =259 | year =1964  | pages = 45&ndash;48}}</ref><ref>{{citation | first =Edmond| last =Bonan  |authorlink=Edmond Bonan|title =Sur les G-structures de type quaternionien| journal = Cahiers de Topologie et Géométrie Différentielle Catégoriques| volume =9 | year =1967| issue =4 | pages = 389&ndash;463| url = http://archive.numdam.org/ARCHIVE/CTGDC/CTGDC_1967__9_4/CTGDC_1967__9_4_389_0/CTGDC_1967__9_4_389_0.pdf }}.</ref> which is ''torsion free'', if and only if, "two" of the almost complex structures <math>I, J, K</math> are integrable and in this case the manifold is hypercomplex.

== Twistor spaces ==
There is a 2-dimensional sphere of quaternions
<math>L\in{\mathbb H}</math> satisfying <math>L^2=-1</math>.
Each of these quaternions gives a complex
structure on a hypercomplex manifold ''M''. This
defines an almost complex structure on the manifold
<math>M\times S^2</math>, which is fibered over
<math>{\mathbb C}P^1=S^2</math> with fibers identified with <math>(M, L)</math>. 
This complex structure is integrable, as follows
from Obata's theorem (this was first explicitly proved by 
[[Dmitry Kaledin]]<ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Kaledin 
|first=Dmitry |author-link=Dmitry Kaledin |eprint=alg-geom/9612016 
|title=Integrability of the twistor space for a hypercomplex manifold |date=1996 }}</ref>). This complex manifold
is called the [[twistor space]] of <math>M</math>.
If ''M'' is <math>{\mathbb H}</math>, then its twistor space
is isomorphic to <math>{\mathbb C}P^3\backslash {\mathbb C}P^1</math>.
